label: text
text: The Czecho-Slovakia Government has granted an annual subsidy of 15,000 gold francs (£600) to the International Institute of Intellectual Co-operation.

label: text
text: The Hungarian Government has restored to the French authorities the aeroplane in which the brothers Arrachée nudvertently landed in Hungary.

label: text
text: The New South Wales State Government is showing itself inimical to the policy of the new Seattlers' League formed to facilitate Immigration, and has withdrawn the subsidy.

label: text
text: It is stated that there is a probability of that remarkable old Chinese play. "The Circle of Chai," being seen in London, in a new English version during the coming season.

label: text
text: The Diocesan Boys' School re-opens on Monday, at 9 a.m. Parents and guardians can see the Heal's master in the school office from 0 to 11 a.m. to-morrow. New bovs should attend to-mormow at 9 a.m.

label: text
text: About 80th Chinese, residents of Limchouse-causeway, Pennyfield, West Indin Dock-street, and Highstreet, Poplar, accompanied, in some cases, by their English wives, enjoyed a trip into the country on August 7, travelling by char-a-bane to Kingston, and thence by boat to Windsor. Among the party were several members of the independent Massonie order, together with members of the Ancient Order of Bruids.

label: text
text: Lt. Col. P. T. Ethelton, late British Consul-Cigneral in Turkestan, in an article in the Daily Graphic, attributes Soviet Russia's non-acceptance of the invitation to be represented on the Opium Commission to the existence of poppy, plantations in Russian Turkestan, the existence of which has been cleverly concealed, and from which the Bolsheviks derive so lucrative an income. The frontier of Russian Turkestan marches with that of Western China.

label: text
text: The Anderson Music Co., Ltd. announce their latest list of new process records. There is a nice variety for different tastes.

label: text
text: A fresh case of enteric fever (typhoid) was notified on Thursday. The patient is a Chinese from the city district.

label: text
text: For sitting on the steps of the Cenotaph, which was recently made an offence by Government notification, a coolie was fined $3 by Major C. Willson at the Central Magistracy yesterday.

label: text
text: Further evidence was taken at the Kowloon Magistruey yesterday in a charge of manslaughter against a sanitary coolie. It was alleged that he caused the death of a hawker by prodding him with a bamboo broom. The case will be continued this afternoon.

label: text
text: The Eastern Extension Telegraph Co., notifies that telegraphie communication with Hankow is totally interrupted. Telegrams to Hankow and places beyond are now being transmitted by wire from Shanghai to Wuhu and thence by post. They are subject to heavy delay and are accepted at sender's risk only.

label: text
text: Mrs. Hayley Morriss, who is to be released from Holloway Gaol, was sentenced to nine months' imprisonment in December last for conspiring with her husband—who was sentenced to two years' hard labour and twelve months' imprisonment for offences against young girls. Mrs. Morriss's release is on account of a remission of two months for good behaviour. During his imprisonment Morris's estate, Pippingford Park, has been in the charge of a friend.

label: text
text: In connection with the reported discovery of giant Monitor lizards in the Dutch islands of the East Indies, the Times publishes a photograph of the Two-Banded Monitor now in the London Zoo, which is 7 ft. 7 in. long. But the Banded Monitor is insignificant compared to the giant lizard of the same genus, which has been known to a few zoologists and to a few Dutch officials and sportsmen since 1912. These creatures, found on the island of Komodo, are said to attain the length of 30 ft., and to be extremely dangerous to man.

label: text
text: British Museum acquisitions include a Japanese panel painting showing a figure portrait, which is probably seventeenth-century work, and four fine colour prints. One of the principal of these is by an artist named Kiyonaga and another is by the author better-known Hokusai.

label: text
text: Paris, July 30.—A few weeks ago a patient in hospital at Tarbes accidentally swallowed a tube containing radium to the value of 30,000 francs. The obvious measures for its recovery proved unavailing. The patient has now died, but an examination of the body has failed to reveal the missing object.

label: text
text: The wife of the Russian General Ataman Semienoff, has been arrested in Paris on a charge of fraudulently converting to her own use of funds and other articles obtained by her on credit. A young Pole, named Langehewski, is being charged as an accomplice.

label: text
text: "Moscow," August 27.—The strike of the employees of the Indo-European Telegraph Company continues. London is working India via the "Eastern Telegraph Company, paying daily over £500. The five days' strike has caused the concessionaries a loss of £25,000, whereas the salary raise demanded by the staff amounts to only £1,350 per annum.—Rengo.

label: text
text: Mr. and Mrs. E. Thursby-Pelham were among the passengers who arrived by the s.s. "Taiping" from Australia yesterday

label: text
text: The giant arum of. Sumatra, which produces a leaf one year and a flower the next year, is in full bloom at Kew Gardens and is attracting much attention not only for its size, but for its beauty.

label: text
text: Chicago, August 13.—The zoological section of the Capt. Marshall Field Brazilian Expedition obtained during its first week, a wolf-spider, a mouse-oppossum of a species hitherto not represented in an American museum, and many other valuable specimens to the number of 300. This was reported to D. C. Davies, director of Field Museum of Natural History here, from which the explorers departed for Tuama recently, Mrs. Field is taking an active part in the work, a communication stated, accompanying George K. Cherrie, leader, each morning on collecting expeditions.

label: text
text: The principal Japanese delegates to the League Assembly at Geneva are $ ^{c} $ Viscount Ishii, Mr. Kenzb Adachi and Mr. R. Nagni.

label: paragraph_title
text: SOCIAL AND PERSONAL NEWS.

label: text
text: Mr. W. H. Daukes and Lt. Col. A. E. D. Anderson, D.S.O., M.C., directors of the Anglo-Dutch Plantations "of Java, Ltd., have left London for Java on a visit to the company's properties.

label: text
text: The late Mr. William Montague Hammett Kirkwood (76), of Newbridge House, Bath, barrister-at-law, at one time Legal Adviser to the Japanese Government, left unsettled estate valued at £3,373 (net personality, £3,082).

label: text
text: The wedding of Miss Dorothy Muriel Holyoak and Capt. C. D. Armstrong, M.C., East Surrey Regiment, has been fixed for October 16. After the service at St. John's Cathedral there will be a reception at Government House.

label: text
text: Mr. D. J. Jones, a young Pontard-dawe schoolmaster, was chaired as the "Bard of the Annual Welsh National" Eisteddfodd at Swanseon August 5, winning the prize for an ode entitled "The Monk". Led to the platform between two of the Bards, he was instilled in the chair which was part of the prize, and which was a fine example of Chinese carved work, the gift of the Welsh Colony in Shanghai.

label: text
text: The Chinese Delegation to the Seventh Assembly of the League of Nations is as follows: First Delegate: H.E. Mr. Chao-Hsin-chu, Envoy Extraordinary and Minister Plenipotentiary in Italy; Second Delegate: H.E. Mr. Wang King-ky, Envoy Extraordinary and Minister Plenipotentiary in Belgium. The Third Delegate has not yet been appointed. Mr. Chao-hsin, Chu was Chinese Acting Minister in London 1822-1925.

label: text
text: The American Minister to Peking, Mr. J. V. A. MacMurray, accompanied by Mrs. MacMurray and Mr. and Mrs. Peck and daughter, of Peking, will pass through Hong Kong about the latter part of the month on route to Manila. Mr. and Mrs. MacMurray will spend part of their vacation with Governor-General and Mrs. Wood. The party will probably visit U.S. Consul-General and Mrs. Jenkins, at Canton, and will merely be in the Colony for a few days. Reuter.

label: text
text: Tsinanfu, September 3.—Mr. Kang Yu-wei, “modern sage of China,” arrived at Tsinanfu from Tsingtao on the night of September.

label: text
text: The Council of the Society of Incorporated Accountants and Auditors have elected Mr. Thomas Keens as president, and Mr. Henry Morgan as vice-president for the ensuing year.

label: text
text: Matheson Lang bade farewell to London at the King's Theatre, Hammersmith, in "The Chinese Bungalow," and will not be seen again in the metropolis till his return, late in March next, from his Canadian tour.

label: text
text: Mr. Percival, A. R. Leith, chief civil and mechanical engineer, Smith's Deck Company, Limited, South Shields, has been appointed chief engineer to the River Tees Conservancy Commissioners, and will take up his new appointment on October 1.

label: text
text: The death is announced, in his 80th year, at Schonenwerd, of M. Edward Bailly-Prior, senior director of Bailly. Limited, one of the largest shoemaking firms in the world, who was a member of the Swiss National Council from 1902 to 1917.

label: text
text: Being held responsible for the assault case of Mr. Chao Chin-pa, an adviser to Marshal Chang T8-lin, by the Fengtian authorities, Mr. Wang Yung-pao, the Chinese Minister to Tokyo, has applied to the Waichiaopu for his return home for recuperation.

label: text
text: Shanghai, September 2.—Sergeant Short was one of the principals yesterday afternoon at a ceremony at Holy Trinity Cathedral when he and Miss Mary Hoffman were married in the presence of a small gathering of friends. The ceremony was performed by the Rev. A. C. S. Trivott, Sub-Dean.

label: paragraph_title
text: 답변

label: text
text: Mr. Stewart Becker and Mr. Stuart Allen, who were graduated from Princeton University in the class of 1926, have arrived in Peking to teach English on the faculty of the Y.M.C.A. School of Finance and Commerce. Both young men were active in their undergraduate days, taking positions of leadership in student affairs. In his Senior year Becker was manager of the Princeton Commons, a dining hall for 1,200 students. They are living with Mr. Robert R. Garloy, former General Secretary of the Y.M.C.A. in Peking.

label: text
text: Mr. Robert Hyde Greg, formerly British Minister to Siam, arrived in Bucharest on August 9 to take up his duties as Minister Romania.

label: text
text: The Lord and Lady Montagu of Béaulieu had the honour of being invited to luncheon with the Queen on board the Royal Yacht at Cowes Roads on August 6.

label: text
text: Messrs. M. Honjo, K. Kawase, S. Kuboto, A. Munago and I. Watonabe arrived at Southampton on August 10 from New York on board the Cunard liner "Aquitania."

label: text
text: The Diploma in Tropical Medicine and Hygiene of the Royal Colleges of Physicians and Surgeons of England has been conferred on W. Z. C. Yuen, M.B., B.S., Hong Kong.

label: text
text: The Marquess and Marchioness of Reading left London on August 10 for Scotland, where they will be the guests of Viscount and Viscountess Inchcape at Glenapp Castle, Ballantrae.

label: text
text: Baron Fukushima and Count Sano, of Japan, are among the scoutmasters of eight nations who commenced an annual course of scoutcraft at Gilwell Park, Essex, on August 6.

label: text
text: Recent Colonial Office appointments include the "following:~Mr. M. P. O'Connor, M.B., Ch.B., etc., as Medical Officer," Malaya; and Miss P. J. Smith, as Nursing Sister, Straits Settlements.

label: text
text: Mrs. Margaret Proctor Smith, the well-known singer and lecturer who engaged in volunteer mission work in Wuchang until last year when she left for America for a visit, turned to Hankow a few days ago. She will be with Dr. and Mrs. Bliss part of September, and then go to Ichang to visit Dr. and Mrs. Luten of the U.S. Navy, in October, returning to Hankow for a two weeks' visit to Deaconess Hart, after which she will make her home in Hankow.

label: text
text: Simla, August 22.—It is understood that Lala Laj Patrai, the well-known leader of the Punjab Hindus, has resigned from the Swaraj Party owing to serious differences with Pandit Motilal Nehru, and intends to join the Responsive Co-operation Party to be led by Pandit Malaviya, the All-India Hindu leader. Lala Laj Patrai's resignation, though not confirmed, is regarded as a great blow to the Swarajist organisation on the eve of the General Elections.

text: A WEEK'S PAPERS IN ONE.

label: paragraph_title
text: OVERLAND CHINA MAIL.

label: text
text: Outstanding events of the week up to this Wednesday (inclusive) are graphically described in the Overland China Mail.

label: text
text: People at Home want to know all about the historic occurrences concerning sojourners in China. Better than writing a letter is to send along a copy with all the news.

label: paragraph_title
text: OUR NAVAL CASUALTIES.

label: text
text: The events leading up to the Naval action on the Yangtse, details of the casualties suffered by the British in an heroic attempt to uphold prestige, will be found in this week's issue, together with names of ships taking part and other information.

label: paragraph_title
text: PICKETS AS PIRATES.

label: paragraph_title
text: WARS IN CHINA.

label: text
text: Prominence is now given by Home papers to the struggles in China, and the effect on foreign intercourse. Friends will be asking themselves questions. Not a cable from the daily publication has been omitted. Such tell the folks what they want to know. Despatches regarding the epic defence of Wuchang will give readers an inkling into methods of Chinese warfare. Wu Pei-fu's "death," "capture" and his real condition will also prove interesting.

label: text
text: Colony's loss: The death of another well-known resident, in Dr. J. C. Dalmahoy Allan, is recorded.

label: text
text: “Mutiny” on ship: What happened on a Hong Kong bound vessel, the “Talamba,” when deportees gave the officers an anxious time, is told in full.

label: text
text: All the local news of the week: All the local news is included in the Overland China Mail every week, out on Fridays in time for the mail.

label: text
text: A host of unique events in and around the Colony—combining to let others know about life in the Far East—will be found. To mention only a few:—Reception to Prince Dahni and Princess Sipbam of Siam; Hong Kong as the "Island of Kisses" in a film taken here; Canton's decision to hand back mission hospitals; the Governor being entertained by Chinese; Hobbs's reply to local cricketers.
